limits.statement: At the base commit no stable entry point selects the cache index or the scheduler. The only file outside lib/artifact-store-next, lib/scan-scheduler-next and test/perf-next that holds an import line naming either directory (references, recomputed with git grep at the base commit) is a T19 invariants test, which imports createArtifactStore from store.mjs to check read-time integrity. scanners/index.mjs (runScan) and bin/bskel.mjs are not in that list. runLegacyScanCached and runProjectGraphCached run beside the stable scan as shadows, and nothing outside the layer calls them; an import with a computed path would not match the pattern. The old advisory measurement file says the same: "no persistent cache wired into stable runScan".

The files listed under references, outside lib/artifact-store-next, lib/scan-scheduler-next and test/perf-next, contain the text artifact-store-next or scan-scheduler-next at the base commit (recomputed with git grep): the T19 wave-2 mutation record and mutation catalogue (the catalogue holds find and replace text of lines in cache-key.mjs, invalidation.mjs and store.mjs, so those lines are coupled to files that T19 owns), the T19 invariants test, the T00 ownership map, the nested runner and the draft project-graph RFC. The CI workflow and test/package-install.test.mjs are not in the list; CI reaches the layer only through the nested runner step T21 perf-next.

The root test script is node --test test/*.test.mjs, which matches test files directly under test/ and not test/perf-next. The suite runs through node scripts/run-next-nested-tests.mjs T21 (CI job nested-next, step T21 perf-next) or through node --test on its test files (the direct-tap command), so a green root npm test is not T21 evidence.

package.json lists lib/ in its files array (references), so both source directories are part of the npm package. test/package-install.test.mjs packs and installs the package and runs the installed bskel binary, but it is not among the files that name either directory (see layer-mentioned-outside-its-directories), so no test at the base commit imports a module of the layer from a packed and installed copy. This record runs the layer from an extracted copy of the base commit, not from a packed artifact.

No timing measurement at an exact commit on a supported platform; no SLO. The only timing file, test/perf-next/baselines/2026-09-25-container.json (pinned in files with its sha256 and never edited), is labelled "advisory-measurement-not-slo", was measured on 2026-09-25 in an environment that the file itself describes as "assistant container; not a supported-platform certification" (v22.16.0, Linux 6.18.44 x86_64), and names the implementation branch scale/t21/incremental-store, which is a branch name and not a commit. Its caveats, copied verbatim: "synthetic generated files only"; "warm means a second same-process full rehash, not a cache hit"; "timings are not release SLOs"; "stable scanner adapters still perform their existing discovery/read paths". No timing or memory figure of that file is copied or asserted by this record.

In the old advisory file warm is a second full rehash in the same process: test/perf-next/benchmark.mjs labels it same-process-second-pass-no-cache-yet and never consults the cache index. The legacy cache benchmark (legacy-cache-benchmark.mjs) leaves peak RSS out on purpose and states that a cache hit still rebuilds the content index before the key lookup, so a hit is not a skip of reading the tree. The fixture below replays only the source digest of the smallest old workload (no timing): it equals the digest that the old file recorded, which shows that the old workload can be regenerated, not how fast it ran.

The pinned smoke test (t21-benchmark-smoke.test.mjs) runs the legacy cache benchmark for the javascript-express adapter only, with --samples 1 and --profile-id ci-smoke-unapproved, and asserts that the reported figures are finite and non-negative and that the semantic check holds, not how large they are. The equivalence test (t21-legacy-cache-equivalence.test.mjs) runs all five stable adapters through cache off, miss and hit without timing. No pinned test times more than that one adapter once.

evaluatePerformanceGate (performance-policy.mjs) measures nothing: it compares candidate reports that a caller supplies. Nothing in the layer produces the approved external peak-RSS measurements that legacy-cache-benchmark.mjs names as the condition for leaving BLOCKED ("performance gate must remain BLOCKED until approved external peak-RSS measurements are supplied"), and no SLO exists. The fixture records only the decisions that stop before any figure is compared (identity, workload, sample and semantic checks): blocked, fail or refusal, never pass.

createCacheIndex checks that its index path stays inside the repository root with path.resolve and path.relative only, without realpath. A directory inside the root that is a symlink to a directory outside it is therefore followed and the index file is written outside the root (first fixture). Paths that leave the root lexically, and digests and refs that would leave the store root, are refused (second fixture). A caller that needs containment against symlinks has to check it itself.

runProjectGraphCached accepts a project root after path.resolve and path.relative only: project-cache-runner.mjs holds no realpath (the baseline test checks the pinned text). A project root that is a symlink inside the repository to a directory outside it is therefore scanned: the run passes and the indexed files are those of the outside tree (first fixture, field through_the_link). A root that leaves the repository lexically is refused with the message "project root escapes repository" (same fixture, last field; project-graph-cached-run-refusals records the same refusal). This is the same lexical check as in cache-index-containment-is-lexical, and a caller that scans trees it does not trust has to refuse symlinks itself. Not recorded: a symlink to a file, symlinks below a project root, and any fix.

The legacy scan cache key holds file digests and no repository location, so a copy of a tree together with its cache hits the cache entry of the original, and the report that is served still names the tree it was created in. A consumer that needs the paths of the tree it asked about cannot use a served report as it is. The fixture records the booleans and the fields that carry the path, never a path.

The file index skips every directory named .git, .sbf, node_modules, .venv, venv, __pycache__, coverage, dist or build, at any depth (DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRS in file-index.mjs, listed in the fixture), and the cache key of runLegacyScanCached holds the digest of that index as its only source digest. The python-fastapi adapter lists the files it reads with ripgrep and four exclusion globs of its own, for .venv, site-packages, node_modules and __pycache__ (references), so it reads Python files under venv, coverage, dist and build that the index never hashes. After one new router file was added under each of those four names, the source digest and the cache key did not move, and the cached call was a hit that served the report from before the change, while an uncached call reported the new route (fixture, field excluded_names). Under .git, .sbf, node_modules, .venv and __pycache__ the adapter does not read the new file either, so the cached report stays right; under a name the index reads (field control_a_name_the_index_reads) the digest moved and the call missed. Only the python-fastapi adapter was run: other adapters list their files with other exclusion rules, so which names are affected depends on the adapter. No fix is recorded.

A legacy cache entry is keyed by the digest of the whole file index and the other key terms, so a changed source state gives another entry and the earlier entry stays in place: in the control of legacy-cache-stale-hit-in-an-excluded-directory, two source states left two index entries and two references to artifacts from the index. In legacy-scan-cache-shadow, for its fixed input, a second set of search terms left two index entries and two blobs in the store. These counts are for those fixed inputs and not a rule: reachableArtifactRefs counts references and is not a blob count, and the store keeps one blob per digest (store-layout-and-refs), so two entries whose artifacts have equal bytes name the same blob. Collection protects every artifact that the index references (gc-keeps-referenced-artifacts), so garbage collection does not reclaim those. cache-index.mjs offers remove and invalidateDependencies, but neither runLegacyScanCached nor runProjectGraphCached calls either (the baseline test checks the pinned text of both modules), so entries stay until a caller retires them. No retention policy, size limit or eviction is recorded.

collectArtifactGarbage takes no lock: lib/lock.mjs guards the cache index (set, remove, invalidateDependencies) and the garbage collector does not use it. No pinned test runs a put concurrently with an applied collection, so what happens to a blob that is stored between the scan of the roots and the delete is not recorded. The age rule compares the modification time of a blob with the nowMs argument (default: the current time): a blob stamped after nowMs counts as young even for a minimum age of zero. The fixtures pass a fixed nowMs; with the default, the same call depends on the clock.

runTaskGraph (scheduler.mjs) has no timeout, cancellation or retry: the source holds no timer and no abort signal (the baseline test checks the pinned text), so a task that never settles occupies its slot for the life of the run, and a worker error is recorded as the failure of that task and blocks its dependents (fixture).

buildProjectCachePlan and runProjectGraphCached take the project graph as plain data of the draft schema sbf.project-graph/draft-1. scanners/project-graph/INTERFACE_RFC.md (the file listed under references) states the status "draft / provisional, not a stable SBF contract" and that this layer consumes the graph as plain data. The fixtures use hand-written graph objects, not the output of the project-graph builder, so their agreement is not recorded here.

No consumer, runner or provider integration of the scheduler and the store is recorded. By the import search in stable-scan-does-not-use-the-layer nothing outside the layer calls them (a computed import path would not match), and the nested runner only runs and counts the test files of the suite. The combination of consumers, runner, provider and packed artifact belongs to audit item T21-05 and is not claimed here.

No rollback plan, supported-scope record or approvable promotion evidence is recorded for the layer; those belong to audit item T21-06 and are not claimed here. The schema identifiers of the layer (sbf.*/1 and the /draft-1 identifiers of the project graph and the project cache plan) are recorded as they stand and are not promoted by this record.

Every output hash and count was generated on the machine named in environment (one operating system, one CPU architecture) and replayed there on two Node majors; no other platform was run. The fixtures listed here run a stable adapter and need ripgrep (rg) on PATH, which the stable adapters call; without it the replay fails with a message and is never skipped. The version of ripgrep is named in environment and is not compared.

Every fixture input is a small tree or literal data written by the scenario module, or one of the pinned fixture projects; no real repository, no large tree and no concurrent load is replayed. Scale, timing and memory behaviour are not recorded.

The pinned modules load ajv (scanners/registry.mjs validates adapter descriptors), so the replays run against the node_modules of the checkout once the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages equals the version that package-lock.json states at the base commit. The files inside the installed packages are not hashed.

test/perf-next/baseline-scenarios.mjs, the module that every fixture calls, belongs to the PR that adds this record and is not hashed: the base commit does not hold it, and a hash would force a new record for every edit of a comment. It is bound only by the output hash and the expected values of the fixtures that call it, so a change that alters an output is reported and a change that alters none is not.

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every fixture output hash and every expected value, the reference lists of the limits that carry them, the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages against package-lock.json at the base commit, the quotations from the old advisory measurement file and from the benchmark scripts that the limits make (compared with the pinned text), and the per-file table, every test count, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit that INTERFACE_RFC.md and the store README state are compared by baseline-record.test.mjs with the values it recomputed, never with a copy kept in the documents.
levels: always: the record is well formed, and any single tampered hash, size, test count, exit code, expected value, limit status or commit id is reported; artifact_digest covers every field except its own value, so an edit of a limit statement, a fixture class, a call, a title or this text that is not re-sealed is reported

live files: size, sha256 and blob id of every pinned file are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, and so is a non-markdown file in lib/artifact-store-next, lib/scan-scheduler-next or test/perf-next that the record neither pins nor names as an own file; drift skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent; the tree id equals base_tree; the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; the directory listings of both source directories, the test directory and the input directories equal the pinned files; the suite entry of the nested runner at that commit names the recorded source and test directories; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit (node_modules linked from the checkout once the installed versions equal environment.loaded_packages, which package-lock.json at the base commit states; the scenario module of this record is copied in) and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output
references: the files outside the track directories that match each recorded pattern are recomputed with git grep at the pinned commit and must equal the list in the limit

documents: the per-file table, every "<n> tests" figure, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit in INTERFACE_RFC.md and the store README describe the pinned base commit and are compared with this record, whose counts and first runner line the commands level reproduces
not_recomputed: ci_observations: read once from the CI API (gh api, read-only) and kept for traceability; no test re-reads them
environment: describes the machine this record was generated on; the ripgrep version is informational (ripgrep must be installed, its version is not compared)

prose: limit statements, fixture origins, the title and this text are bound only by artifact_digest, which reports an edit that is not re-sealed; an editor who re-seals the record is caught only by review of the diff and by the recomputed values above
the files inside the installed packages that the pinned files load (environment.loaded_packages): not hashed; only their versions are compared with package-lock.json at the base commit
support data: the inputs of the fixtures are synthetic (written by the scenario module) or pinned fixture projects; their values are not independently checked
the scenario module test/perf-next/baseline-scenarios.mjs: an own file of the PR, not hashed; bound only by the fixture output hashes and expected values

INTERFACE_RFC.md and the store README: only the numbers and the base commit named above are recomputed, not the explanatory text; t21-interface-rfc.test.mjs compares the names, constants and vocabularies of the RFC with the code of the working tree separately
